activity_context.topic_title: The Curvature of a Plane Curve

feedback.problem:
The signed curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,t⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{}{\sqrt{(1+{t}^{2})^{3}}},\,t>0.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,y(t)=t.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =-{t}^{-1},\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =1 \\ {x}^{″}(t) & ={t}^{-2},\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(t) & =\frac{-{t}^{-1}\cdot 0-1\cdot ({t}^{-2})}{{((-{t}^{-1})^{2}+(1)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-{t}^{-2}}{{({t}^{-2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-{t}^{-2}\cdot ({t}^{2})^{3/2}}{{(1+{t}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-{t}^{-2}\cdot |t{|}^{3}}{{(1+{t}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-{t}^{-2}\cdot {t}^{3}}{{(1+{t}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-t}{\sqrt{(1+{t}^{2})^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we removed the absolute value because $t>0.$
